deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the notes are working with derivators D (axioms Der 1–Der 5, 5'), the cohomology H^i_D(X, ξ) of a small category X with coefficients ξ ∈ D(X), and the class W_D of 'D-equivalences'. The previous page asks for the converse implication i ∈ W_D ⇒ i^t ∈ W_D. Grothendieck observes that this needs a Mayer–Vietoris square to be cocartesian in cohomology, and not merely cartesian.

The geometric input is a category X covered by two 'opens' (sieves/cosieves) U, U' with X = U ∪ U'. This cover is encoded by a functor X → Q = Δ^1 × Δ^1. The associated diagram Ψ_Q(X) of type Q in Cat has as fibres the comma categories X_{/q}. On this page he notes that the fourth fibre is X̄_{(1,1)} = X_{/(1,1)} ≃ X. So Ψ_Q(X) is just the square of inclusions U∩U' → U → X, U∩U' → U' → X.

The essential property of this square, among those already seen, is the following. The canonical functor from the Grothendieck construction ∫(U ← U∩U' → U') to X, given by the arrows of the diagram V → U → X, V → U' → X with V = U∩U', is in W. Equivalently, the homotopy pushout (computed as a Grothendieck construction, as in Thomason's theorem) of U ← U∩U' → U' is weakly equivalent to X.

He then abstracts this as 'Principe (P)'. Take any diagram X_0 → X_a, X_0 → X_b in Cat of shape Ψ = Q minus one vertex. Let 𝒳 → Ψ be the cofibred category it defines. For ξ ∈ D(𝒳), set γ = K_* φ_*(ξ) ∈ D(Q), where φ: 𝒳 → Ψ is the projection and K: Ψ → Q the inclusion (this is on the next page). The vertices of γ are the cohomologies of X_0, X_a, X_b and 𝒳. γ is cartesian by construction. The principle asserts that, because 𝒳 is cofibred over Ψ, γ is also cocartesian. This is a homotopy-pushout (Mayer–Vietoris / descent) property of cohomology with coefficients in a derivator. On the next page he suspects it does not follow from Der 1–5, 5' and proposes it as a provisional axiom 'Der 6'. The purpose is to prove that W_D has the closure properties of a basic localizer.
errors: As stated for an arbitrary derivator, 'Der 6' (cartesian ⇒ also cocartesian for the cohomology square of a cofibred 𝒳 over the corner) is false in non-stable derivators.

Counterexample in the homotopy derivator of spaces: take X_0 = two points and X_a = X_b = a point, so that 𝒳 ≃ S^1. Take ξ constant with value a discrete 2-point space K. The square has vertices LK ≃ K (2 points), K, K and K×K (4 points). The homotopy pushout of the corner K ← LK → K is 2 points, not K×K, so the square is not cocartesian.
So the property is really a stability/additivity condition (cohomology as H^i in a triangulated-type setting). In a stable derivator it is automatic, since there cartesian ⇔ cocartesian.
Grothendieck's suspicion that it is not deducible from Der 1–5 is correct for general derivators; it would follow from a stability axiom.

ideas.what: Covering a category by two sieves U, U' gives a square in Cat whose Grothendieck construction ∫(U ← U∩U' → U') → X is a weak equivalence (Mayer–Vietoris for categories)
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy pushout of an open cover / excision for sieves; Thomason's hocolim = Grothendieck construction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thomason (1979) for hocolim; Grothendieck/Maltsiniotis/Cisinski in the theory of basic localizers
ideas.where_published: Possibly Pursuing Stacks / Les Dérivateurs (unsure); Maltsiniotis 'La théorie de l'homotopie de Grothendieck' (2005)

ideas.what: Principle (P) / provisional 'Der 6': for 𝒳 cofibred over the corner Ψ, the square K_*φ_*ξ ∈ D(Q) of cohomologies is cocartesian as well as cartesian
ideas.modern_name: Mayer–Vietoris/descent for derivator cohomology; bicartesian squares in stable derivators
ideas.usually_credited_to: Heller (stable homotopy theories, 1988/97); Maltsiniotis, Groth (stable derivators, cartesian ⇔ cocartesian, 2013)
ideas.where_published: Les Dérivateurs (1990–91) discusses Der axioms; a 'Der 6' of this form is not known to me

ideas.what: Class W_D of D-equivalences and the question of whether it is stable under the needed operations (i ∈ W_D ⇒ i^t ∈ W_D)
ideas.modern_name: Localizer associated with a derivator; basic localizers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Pursuing Stacks, Les Dérivateurs); Cisinski, Maltsiniotis

missed.claim: A provisional derivator axiom 'Der 6', distinct from the published Der list, appears here in an early form (archive dated from 1982). It requires cohomology squares of cofibred categories over the corner Ψ to be bicartesian, i.e. a stability-type descent condition. It shows Grothendieck isolating the cartesian-vs-cocartesian issue that later became the definition of stable derivators.
missed.quote: "Principe" (P) Soit X_0 → X_a, X_0 → X_b un diagramme dans Cat de type Ψ, soit 𝒳 la cat. cofibrée sur Ψ qu'il définit
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest for the genesis of derivator axioms and of stability (Heller, Maltsiniotis, Groth). It is mathematically subsumed by the known result that in stable derivators cartesian ⇔ cocartesian, and it is false for unstable derivators.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains a provisional axiom (P)/'Der 6' and a clear Mayer–Vietoris motivation, which is of some historical interest for the early derivator axioms. Mathematically it is either routine (excision for sieve covers) or subsumed by later stable-derivator theory, and it is false in the stated generality.
